newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebels seize Kisangani airport.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels seize Kisangani airport.

text.p: Rebels have seized the heavily defended airport at Zaire's third city of Kisangani, diplomats and relief workers said on Saturday.
Some reports said soldiers from Zaire's notoriously ill-disciplined army had gone on a looting spree in the city, the nerve centre of army operations in the war zone.

"The international airport has already been taken and looting has spread across the city," a senior U.N. official said in Zaire's capital Kinshasa after the rebels launched their assault on Friday evening.

The fall of Kisangani would be the biggest setback for the government since the rebels took up arms in October, vowing to topple veteran President Mobutu Sese Seko. They already hold towns and a large swathe of territory in the east.

A defence ministry spokesman in Kinshasa was unable to give details of the fighting but confirmed that there had been shooting. "The situation is very tense and there is movement in every direction," the spokesman told Reuters.
The government had concentrated soldiers, Serb mercenaries and hardline Rwandan Hutu allies at Kisangani, a major port on the Zaire River before it flows west to Kinshasa.
Aid workers in Kinshasa who were in contact with Kisangani overnight said the fighting started with heavy mortar fire on the north east outskirts on Friday evening.

A regional military source said that two main rebel columns had merged to attack the airport. Zairean soldiers and allied mercenaries had concentrated around the international airport, where military hardware including combat helicopters was based.
"The mercenaries fled the airport but nobody knows where they have gone. Some of the senior military seem to have gone across the river," a senior Western diplomat said on Saturday.

The regional source said frightened civilians from Kisangani's 500,000-strong population were massing near the Zaire river hoping to board barges. "The soldiers are looting Kisangani as they flee. Many are leaving by boats. There is confusion among the citizens," the source added.
Diplomats, aid workers and Western security sources reported shooting in Kisangani itself overnight.
Aid agencies and embassies were looking at ways to evacuate foreign nationals from the city, diplomats and aid workers said. Those waiting included a small group of aid workers.
France, which has troops based in neighbouring Central African Republic, was reported to be looking at ways to help.
Kisangani has a second smaller airport, which is almost in town. It was not immediately clear who controlled that airport.
The Tutsi-led rebels took up arms in October accusing the Zairean authorities of denying them citizenship and preparing to expel them to Rwanda, their ancestral home.
Zaire accuses neighbouring Rwanda, Uganda and Burundi of invading in support of the rebels. All three deny the charge.

The government has accepted a U.N. ceasefire plan. The rebels have resisted diplomatic pressure for a ceasefire, most recently on Thursday during a meeting in Uganda between their leader Laurent Kabila and U.N. special envoy Mohamed Sahnoun.
Mobutu has been out of the country for most of the time since August when he had prostate cancer surgery in Europe. A senior supporter has predicted he will return on Monday.
